title: Pad a sequence and inspect its mask
summary: Padding adds filler tokens to reach a chosen length. An attention mask marks real tokens with 1 and padding with 0 in this encoding.
introduction: Padding adds filler tokens to reach a chosen length. An attention mask marks real tokens with 1 and padding with 0 in this encoding. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain pad a sequence and inspect its mask
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Padding adds filler tokens to reach a chosen length. An attention mask marks real tokens with 1 and padding with 0 in this encoding.

blocks.code:
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from tokenizers.models import WordLevel
from tokenizers.pre_tokenizers import Whitespace

tokenizer = Tokenizer(WordLevel({"[PAD]": 0, "[UNK]": 1, "moon": 2, "glows": 3}, unk_token="[UNK]"))
tokenizer.pre_tokenizer = Whitespace()
tokenizer.enable_padding(length=4, pad_id=0, pad_token="[PAD]")
encoded = tokenizer.encode("moon glows")
print(encoded.ids, encoded.attention_mask)
blocks.title: Pad a sequence and inspect its mask

blocks.text: The output is [2, 3, 0, 0] [1, 1, 0, 0]. Two real tokens are followed by two padding tokens. The mask distinguishes them.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Encode only moon and predict the four mask values.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Padding does not shorten an overlong sequence; truncation is a separate choice.
